To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TH-only-immunoreactive, non-CAnergic neurons in the brain are not stained with the GTP cyclohydroxylase I antiserum.
transiently TH-only-ir non-CAnergic neurons in the wild mouse and the hTHTG mouse are not GCH-ir.

transient TH-only-ir non-CAnergic neurons do not produce dihydrxyphenylalanin, and that these neurons are present in some brain regions where CAnergic terminal fibers but not cell bodies exist in adult wild mouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of a new function of TH.
the discovery of a new role of the TH gene in the brain.
the discovery of the non-catechalaminergic function of TH in some regions of the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TH expression does not always mean CAnergic neuron, but it can be a marker for non-CAnergic neurons.

the transiently TH-only-ir non-CAnergic neurons in the postnatal wild mice and the TH-only-ir brain regions in the hTTHg mice are not CAnergic, but they may have some unknown function of TH, because they do not contain BH4.
these non-CAnergic TH-only-ir cells do not synthesize catecholamines but do not exclude the possibility of synthesizing other compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TH is not always a rate-limiting enzyme, and TH is also involved in a non-enzyme function in some neurons.
the TH-only-ir, non-CAnergic neurons may be involved in the regulation of TH gene expression, and that the TH-only-immunoreactivity may be a marker of TH gene expression.
the TH-only-ir non-CAnergic neurons in the brain are not involved in catecholamine production and that the TH-only-immunostaining in the brain is not a marker for the presence of the BH4 cofactors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TH can be used as a marker for neurons in the central nervous system.
the TH enzyme can be expressed independently of its cofactor, BH4, in neurons that are not catecholaminergic.
the expression of the TH enzyme does not always indicate the presence of CAnergic neurons.
